inspiration.source_location: the `insert into t(a) values(3),(1) on duplicate key update a=4` statement: a key-conflicting row whose update moves the conflicting key, after which later statements must find the row under its new key
inspiration.observed_pattern: An ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE assignment that changes the conflicting key itself leaves the stored row identifiable only by the new key; any later statement targeting that key must resolve the moved row or it duplicates
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to a single-row ledger: one upsert moves the primary key from 1 to 11, and a second no-op upsert (note = note) targets the moved key, so a correct engine reports zero affected rows and a single final row while an engine that loses the moved key inserts a duplicate

fixture_notes: One row (id 1, note 10). Step 1 upserts id 1 and moves its primary key to 11 while resetting note. Step 2 upserts id 11 with a no-op assignment, leaving the moved row untouched. The final state is exactly one row keyed 11.
determinism_notes: No clocks, randomness, or concurrency; the final read orders by the unique primary key.
setup: CREATE TABLE ledger (id INT PRIMARY KEY, note INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT INTO ledger (id, note) VALUES (1, 1) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE id = id + 10
INSERT INTO ledger (id, note) VALUES (11, 500) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE note = note
SELECT id, note FROM ledger ORDER BY id
